name: The Met High School Internship Program (Summer)
what_you_do: Work 40 hours over the summer in a Met department such as curatorial, social media, education, imaging or design. You meet museum staff, join a cohort, and go to Teen Fridays. No art background needed.
grades: 10th or 11th grade, or working on a High School Equivalency
who_can_apply: Students in grade 10 or 11, or working on a GED. You must live in and go to school (or home school) in New York, New Jersey, or Connecticut. You need working papers and a Social Security Number or ITIN. A parent or guardian must say yes. You can't have done a Met internship before.
pay_detail: $1,100 stipend when you finish, which the page says matches New York State minimum wage law.
duration: 40 hours, about 10 to 20 hours a week. In 2026: bootcamp July 1, placement July 7 to Aug 7, plus a June 27 family reception.
deadline_text: The 2026 deadline was Friday, March 13, 2026, 5 pm ET, with interview notices by mid-April. 2027 dates are not posted.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form and write short essays. Ask one adult who is not family for a letter. If they pick you, you go to a group interview in person.
notes: You must come to every date on the list. A parent or guardian must come to the party in June. The Met also has a spring internship for New York City students. Connecticut is not a place on this site yet, but students there can apply.
